Implementation Plan Implementation plan: stuck-states P8a-2, clarify and plan emit and park `WAITING:` dependency lines Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8291` @ `c73d8cae33714072fbb5fc5053568bf53f36ea35`. The integration branch does not mismatch. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends dependency_wait_resume.py Scope-mode justification: This issue delivers the rest of Phase 4a in `docs/plans/confine-human-steps-to-activation-plan.md`, as widened by step 2 of P8 in `docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md`. That is: the `WAITING:` prompt rule; parsing it in clarify and plan before `BLOCKED:`; validating the target; and parking the issue in `ai:waiting-on-dependency` with a trusted `AI_DEPENDENCY_WAIT_V1` marker that the P8b resume scan already reads. P8a-1 already registered the label, and P8b already delivered the resume, escalation and seeding. All logic goes into the existing helper `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py`, so the marker schema, target validation and target read stay in one place. The workflows only get a branch inside their existing BLOCKED steps. Two cheap completeness items are included because each is under 30 lines and needs no new interface: - Checking at park time that the target exists, has the right type and is still pending. Without it, a wrong or already-merged target could park an issue for 7 days or loop. - Teaching the P9b clarify retry to accept a `WAITING:` answer. The order of priorities is Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed (§6 Core Priorities in `unattended_system_instructions.md`), and completeness serves correctness. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py` - `scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh` - `scripts/run_plan_codex.sh` - `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` - `.github/workflows/plan.yml` - `prompts/mode-clarify.txt` - `prompts/_templates/mode-clarify.txt` - `prompts/mode-plan.txt` - `prompts/_templates/mode-plan.txt` - `tests/test_dependency_wait_resume.py` - `tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py` - `README.md` - `docs/plans/confine-human-steps-to-activation-plan.md` - `agents.d/stuck-states-p8a2-waiting-parse.md` (new) - `changelog.d/stuck-states-p8a2-waiting-parse.md` (new) ## Automation wiring (§20.E) - **New or extended script:** extends an existing script. `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py` gets two subcommands, `parse-waiting` and `park`. No new script file. - **Entry points:** - `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`: the "Parse Codex output" and "Handle blocked clarification output" steps (triggers: `issues: opened`, `issue_comment` for `/reclarify`). - `.github/workflows/plan.yml`: the `parse_plan` step and the "Handle blocked planning output" step (trigger: `/answer` comment). - Resume stays with P8b's existing `orchestrate_poll.yml` step "Resume dependency waits". - **New long-running supervisor:** none. The poller cron already resumes parked issues. - **DB work:** none. - **Pending-removal registry entry:** none. No single-use script or supervisor is introduced. ## Functions or modules to implement **1. `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py`** (pattern to follow: the existing `scan` subcommand and `seed_blocked`) - `WAITING_LINE_RE`: `^\s*WAITING:\s*(.*\S)\s*$`, case-insensitive like the BLOCKED parsers. The value may be wrapped in one pair of backticks, which is stripped. Accepted grammars, all anchored, with repo matching `REPO_RE`-shaped `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}` and N matching `[1-9][0-9]{0,9}`: - `pr=/#` - `release=shubhodeep1/coding-workflows@stable contains=/#` - `issue=/#` - `parse_waiting(text, repo, issue_number, now) -> dict`: - Takes the first `WAITING:` line outside ```/~~~ fences, using the same toggle as clarify's perl. - Builds the payload `{"kind","repo","number","since":_iso(now)}` and validates it with the existing `_validate_wait`. That enforces: `pr` names the current repo or `UPSTREAM_REPO`; `release` names `UPSTREAM_REPO`, so `contains=` must be upstream; `issue` names the current repo and never this issue. - Also rejects a `pr` target that equals this issue (same repo and number). - Returns one of: - `{"status":"none"}` - `{"status":"disabled","line":L}` when `_resume_enabled()` is false - `{"status":"invalid","reason":,"line":L}` - `{"status":"waiting","kind","repo","number","target":target_label(...),"line":L}` - `L` is the raw value with control characters stripped, cut to 300 characters. - `park(gh, repo, issue_number, kind, target_repo, number, phase, run_url, now) -> str`: 1. Returns `disabled` when `_resume_enabled()` is false. 2. Re-validates through `_validate_wait` plus the self-reference check (`invalid_args`). 3. Reads the target with the existing `fetch_targets(gh, [(target_repo, number)])` (one aliased GraphQL call), then runs the existing `decide(...)` with `released=lambda sha: release_contains(gh, sha, {})` (one REST compare, only for a merged release PR). Mapping: - `waiting` continues. - `resume_answer` or `resume_reclarify` returns `already_resolved`. - `invalid_marker` returns `invalid_target`. - `read_failed` returns `read_failed`. 4. Posts one comment with `gh.comment`; failure returns `comment_failed`. The body contains: - `Waiting on dependency: =#`. For a release the line reads `release=shubhodeep1/coding-workflows@stable contains=...`. - One paragraph saying the issue is parked in `ai:waiting-on-dependency`. The poller posts `/answer` once the dependency lands, or `/reclarify` if it closes unmerged, and escalates after `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_ESCALATE_DAYS` days. To resume sooner, a person replaces the wait label with `ai:blocked` and replies `/answer`. - `Run: `, only when `run_url` matches `^https://\S{1,300}$`. - ``, serialized with `json.dumps(separators=(',',':'))` exactly as `seed_blocked` does, without `"source"`. 5. Calls `gh.add_labels(issue_number, [WAIT_LABEL])`; failure returns `label_failed`. 6. Returns `parked`. - Order matters: the comment goes first, so a wait label never sits without a marker. - `main()` gains two subparsers: - `parse-waiting --output-file F --repo R --issue-number N` prints one JSON line. - `park --repo R --issue-number N --kind K --target-repo TR --number M --phase clarify|plan [--run-url U]` prints `{"status":...,"target":...}`. - Both log `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_PARK op=parse|park issue= target= phase=

outcome= [detail=...]`. - Both always exit 0. An exception yields `{"status":"error"}`, matching the fail-open style of `scan`. - Update the module docstring's batching contract (§14): `park` makes one GraphQL call, at most one compare, one comment and one label write. **2. `scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh`** - Add `dependency_wait_resume.py` to `stage_support_optional_scripts` for the `clarify` and `plan` cases, as P9b did for `clarify_blocked_verify.sh`. - Do not add it to the required lists or to the workflows' `support-scripts-legacy` loops. An older support ref, or legacy mode, must not fail clarify or plan. **3. `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`** - **Inline live prompt, point 9 (around lines 1596-1606) and the output-format block (around line 1650):** add the `WAITING:` rule (text in section 6 below) and an `Or, for a sequencing wait:` / `WAITING: ` alternative. - **"Parse Codex output" (around line 2002):** - Add `env: DEPENDENCY_WAIT_RESUME_ENABLED: ${{ vars.DEPENDENCY_WAIT_RESUME_ENABLED || 'true' }}`. - Before the BLOCKED perl, when `${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR}/dependency_wait_resume.py` is a regular file and not a symlink (the same guard as P9b at around line 1817), run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -I -B ... parse-waiting --output-file "${CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --issue-number "${ISSUE_NUMBER}"` with `|| echo '{"status":"error"}'`. - When the helper is missing, use a perl fallback with the same fence toggle: any unfenced `WAITING:` line gives `status=unparsed`, and the step logs `::warning::DEPENDENCY_WAIT_PARK op=parse outcome=skip reason=helper_missing`. - When `status` is `waiting`, `invalid`, `disabled`, `unparsed` or `error` and a WAITING line exists: - Set `blocked=true`, `needs_clarification=false` and `BLOCKED=true` in the environment. - Set `blocked_reason` and `BLOCKED_REASON` using the existing randomized-delimiter pattern. The reason is `WAITING: ` when `waiting`. Otherwise it is the first unfenced BLOCKED reason if one exists, else `WAITING: `. - Set `waiting=true|false`, plus `waiting_kind`, `waiting_repo` and `waiting_number` only when `status=waiting`. These values are validated tokens and safe to write as single lines. - `exit 0`. - Otherwise write `waiting=false` and continue unchanged. - **"Handle blocked clarification output":** - Add env rows: `WAITING_PARSED`, `WAITING_KIND`, `WAITING_REPO`, `WAITING_NUMBER` from the parse outputs, plus `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_RESUME_ENABLED` and `DEPENDENCY_WAIT_ESCALATE_DAYS` (`vars.... || 'true'` and `|| '7'`). - At the top, when `WAITING_PARSED=true` and the helper passes the guard: 1. `ensure_label_exists "ai:waiting-on-dependency" ... || true`. 2. Run `park ... --phase clarify --run-url "${RUN_URL}"`. 3. On `parked`: run the existing `gh_retry gh issue edit ... --remove-label 'ai:clarification' --remove-label 'ai:planning' --remove-label 'ai:awaiting-approval' --remove-label 'ai:blocked' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`, then `tg_send_tracked "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" "Clarification waiting on dependency for issue #N: ..." "CRITICAL"` (D5 of the confine plan keeps the page), then `exit 0`. 4. Otherwise append ` (dependency wait not parked: )` to `BLOCKED_REASON` and fall through to the unchanged blocked path. - **P
